title: Channel credentialing and listing copy brief
body:
Purpose
---
Working draft: end-to-end credentialing flow + copy brief for cloud marketplaces and channel aggregator partners. Goal: fast technical acceptance + minimal legal friction + high-conversion tile copy for buyer personas (platform engineers, ML leads, and product managers).

Audience
- Internal: GTM, partner ops, legal, finance, product-hosted-api.
- External: Cloud marketplace listing teams, publisher review boards, channel aggregators (ISV shelf vendors).

High-level approach (staged)
1) Pre-flight (internal readiness): ensure SKU mapping, test plan, security artifact pack, and billing metering samples are ready.
2) Credentialing (partner portal): submit tile content + screenshots + support policy + legal statement.
3) Acceptance QA (cloud vendor): pass security/compliance checklist, functional smoke tests, pricing validation.
4) Go-live & monitoring: enable telemetry, usage alerts, tile conversion checks, rollback gating.

Immediate TODOs (short list)
- [ ] Finalize tile title variants for 3 personas (Ravi lead)
- [ ] Create 1-page security pack (Sofia)
- [ ] Generate sample invoices for metering SKU (Finance)
- [ ] Fill in legal answers for data residency and encryption (Legal)
- [ ] Create test harness for listing smoke tests (Eng: release-engineering)

Credentialing checklist (working)
- Account level: partner registration completed, tax form on file, aggregator contract signed (if applicable).
- Technical artifacts: API endpoint for health check, model version manifest, sample request/response pairs (tokenized), latency baseline report (p95/p99), SLA summary (target).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 or equivalent statement, KMS integration notes, data retention policy, PII handling doc, CVE disclosure process.
- Billing/metering: SKU mappings, metering unit definition (per-token vs per-invocation), test usage records, sample invoice line items, subscription vs consumption options.
- Legal & marketing: copy approval sign-off, trademark usage clearance, logo assets (SVG + PNG), privacy policy link + contact.
- UX assets: 3 tile screenshots (dashboard, onboarding flow, cost dashboard), 2 short demo videos (30s), 1 GIF for hero.

Acceptance QA matrix (pass/fail quick checks)
- Functional: API health check returns 200 (YES/NO).
- Billing: example billing event appears in vendor test sandbox (YES/NO).
- Security: security pack uploaded and passes vendor scanner basic checks (YES/NO).
- Copy: title <= 60 chars, description <= 300 chars, benefit bullets 3 items (YES/NO).
- Onboarding: trial provisioning completes in < 10 min (YES/NO).

Tile copy (workshop snippets)
- Title variant A (Platform Engineers): "Redwood Inference — predictable, high-throughput LLM inference"
- Title variant B (ML Leads): "Scale LLM inference with low-latency, cost-aware runtime"
- Short description (300 char draft): "Ship LLM features with consistent performance across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Redwood Inference provides production-grade serving, predictable cost controls, and observability to keep models running fast and reliable."
- Bullets (benefit-oriented):
  - "Low-latency inference with autoscaling GPU pools"
  - "Transparent per-token cost metrics and intelligent batching"
  - "VPC/private deployment options for regulated workloads"
- CTA options: "Start free trial", "Request SLA quote", "View performance benchmarks"

Persona-targeted tile variants (notes)
- Platform Engineer tile: call out API simplicity, health endpoints, and SDKs. Include screenshot of route-level latency breakdown.
- ML Lead tile: emphasize model catalog, quantization suggestions, and quality monitoring/eval hooks. Use A/B test snippet.
- Procurement/Finance tile: focus on predictable reserved capacity pricing, billing examples, and cost-savings from caching/batching.

Risk matrix (high-level)
- Security gating delays — mitigation: pre-submit security pack + internal pen test. Owner: Sofia.
- Billing mismatch in vendor sandbox — mitigation: prepare sample usage traces and escalate to cloud finance contacts. Owner: Ben.
- Copy rejection for trademark/legal — mitigation: prepare alternate phrasing and legal sign-off early. Owner: Ravi.

Approval template (for vendor submission)
- Submitter name: 
- Contact email: 
- Partner account ID: 
- SKU list: (comma separated)
- Tile title chosen: 
- Short description: 
- Group asset links: screenshots, video, logo URLs
- Security pack link: 
- Billing test artifacts attached: Y/N
- Legal clearance: Y/N
- Expected go-live date: 
- Reviewer sign-off: (GTM, Legal, Finance initials)

Acceptance tests - smoke harness (minimum)
- 1. Provision trial tenant via vendor API 
  - Expected: tenant created within 10 min; sample key returned.
- 2. Call API generate endpoint with sample prompt (10 tokens) 
  - Expected: response within p95 latency target, no errors.
- 3. Produce 5 invoice events across 3 different SKUs in vendor sandbox 
  - Expected: each event reflected in sample invoice CSV.
- 4. Run security scanner (basic vendor checklist) against public tile assets
  - Expected: no PII leakage; all links use https.

Notes to self / open questions
- Do we prefer "per-token" metering label or "per-inference" for the initial listing? Finance leaning per-token but vendor UX prefers per-invocation. Needs decision. (Ben)
- How much of the SLA language can be templated vs vendor-specific? Legal to advise.
- Should we include an explicit demo route that triggers the cheapest model variant for trials? Pros: lower cost. Cons: may misrepresent performance. (Ravi)

Checklist for post-launch monitoring
- Enable tile conversion tracking and compare CTR across variants (weekly).
- Set daily alert if provisioning errors > 2% in a 24h window.
- Collect first 7 days of trial usage to validate metering (Finance).
- Prepare rollback playbook: unpublish tile, pause consumption, notify customers.

Reference copy snippets (swap-in friendly)
- Feature-driven short: "Production-grade runtime, predictable economics, and native observability for LLM applications."
- Outcome-driven short: "Reduce inference cost while keeping latency predictable — ship features faster."

Appendix: quick links and artifacts to attach to submission
- latency-report-2025-10.pdf (internal)
- sku-mapping-2025-q4.csv
- security-pack-v1.3.pdf
- demo-gif-hero.gif

Endnotes
- This doc is intentionally informal — capture anything that speeds vendor acceptance. Use linked artifacts and update approval template as we iterate.
- Next sync: Monday standup with Ravi/Sofia/Ben to lock tile title and security pack contents.
